Lets your computers switch Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile data, airplane mode and the hotspot, and press Back, Home and Lock.

With this on, when one of your own computers asks to switch a radio, my-domain opens that switch in Settings and taps it for you, then closes it. Your computers can also press Back, Home, recent apps, notifications and Quick Settings, and lock the screen. While you share this screen with a computer and allow control, it plays that computer’s taps and swipes. It reads the screen only while doing one of these. Nothing works while the phone is locked.

Lets this app ask my-domain to do things on your devices, like ringing or locking your computer or sending it text. It only works while “Let automation apps on this phone use my-domain” is on in my-domain’s Settings, and my-domain tells you each time.
Let apps like Tasker, MacroDroid or Automate ask my-domain to ring or lock your computer, send it text, or run one of your automations. You get a notification each time.
Let automation apps on this phone use my-domain
Apps like Tasker send this key with each request. Keep it private: any app on this phone that has it can use my-domain. Make a new one if it ever leaks.
Copied. It stays on this phone.
The old key stops working at once: put the new one in your automations.
An app that asks Android for my-domain’s automation permission, and that you allow, needs no key. Remove it in Android’s settings for that app (Permissions).

In Tasker, add the action System → Send Intent and fill it in as below (Copy puts it on the clipboard). Fill in Package and Class exactly, and Target: Broadcast Receiver. MacroDroid and Automate have the same fields under Send Intent. The device is its name as shown in my-domain, a nickname you gave it, or its node id.
